answer: No flock may graze the high pasture unless its bell rings the one tone the grazings clerk filed for it, and the clerk tests each bell with a tuning fork every spring. A tundra bell bought from a tinker rings the wrong tone: the willow of the pasture must answer to the filed pitch, and a tinker bell jangles off key. Forging a flock means casting bells for a year, keeping 200 sheep and paying 11,200, while the pulse tone in the clerk's file is sounded at every gathering, so a bell whose tone was never filed is cut from the ewe's neck.
